newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Japan foreign minister begins regional trip.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign minister begins regional trip.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda arrived in Islamabad on Monday for a two-day visit to Pakistan at the start of a three-nation Asian trip that will also take in India and Malaysia.

On Tuesday, he will begin talks with Pakistani authorities that will focus on strengthening political and economic cooperation and cover regional and international issues, Pakistani and Japanese sources said.
Pakistan is "very important" for Japan as a moderate Islamic country and a gateway to Central Asia, a spokesman for Ikeda told reporters after the foreign minister's arrival from Tokyo.

Spokesman Nobuaki Tanaka said Ikeda might urge both India and Pakistan to settle their dispute over the Himalayan region of Kashmir through talks and raise non-proliferation of nuclear and other weapons of mass destruction, which he described as an issue of "real concern to us".

"We appeal to both countries to exercise self-restraint, to become party to the CTBT (Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty), IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) and commit yourselves to safeguards system within IAEA," he said.
He said Ikeda would also discuss during the trip ways to end the civil war in Afghanistan, proposed U.N. Security Council reforms and environmental issues.
He ruled out the possibility of Japan mediating between India and Pakistan on Kashmir, over which the two neighbours have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
But he said: "We will like to be a useful element in the dispute. We will offer our view."
Japan is the largest donor of bilateral Official Development Assistance (ODA) to India and Pakistan, according to an official Japanese statement issued in Islamabad.
"Japan can be very effective from the standpoint of supporting economic reforms by making known its intention to continuously provide economic cooperation in the future," it said.

In Islamabad, Ikeda will hold talks with Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz on Tuesday and pay courtesy calls on President Farooq Leghari and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
Three agreements will be signed during the visit for improvement of bilateral relations and an investment promotion agreement will be initialled, Pakistani sources said.
